newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb to market Roundup tolerant corn.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb to market Roundup tolerant corn.

text.p: DEKALB Genetics Corp said Tuesday it expects to be the first and only seed company marketing Roundup Ready corn to growers for the 1998 growing season, pending final governmental approvals that are anticipated by the end of this year.
Roundup Ready corn is tolerant to glyphosate, the primary active ingredient in Roundup herbicide made by Monsanto Co.

Approvals for commercial use of the seed from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the U.S. Department of Agriculture are expected by the end of this year. The Environmental Protection Agency has already approved the over-the-top use of Roundup Ultra herbicide in corn.

To expedite introduction of the seed, DeKalb said it accelerated breeding and production of the seed to facilitate market introduction in 1997 and delivery in time for the 1998 growing season. To meet the expected demand for Roundup Ready corn, DeKalb said it contracted with commercial growers in Hawaii, Argentina, and Chile.

"In three months, the leading commercial growers in Chile and Argentina will use the Hawaiian-produced parent seed to grow a substantial volume of Roundup Ready seed corn for planting by U.S. growers next spring," said Ken Rinkenberger, DeKalb director of seed marketing, in a news release.

In the meantime, additional testing and research is being conducted this summer to verify the tolerance of DeKalb brand Roundup Ready corn to Roundup Ultra herbicide, as well as appropriate rates and timings of various weed control programs. Roundup Ultra in an enhanced version of Roundup.
"We have high expectations for DeKalb brand Roundup Ready corn hybrids," Rinkenberger said.
DeKalb researches agricultural genetics and biotechnology for seed and swine products.
